papers.title_en: Vision-Language Procedural Reasoning for Context-Aware Reward Modeling of Robotic Endovascular Guidewire Navigation
papers.authors: Wentong Tian, Jiyuan Zhao, Tianliang Yao, Yuxiang Fan, Zhengyu Shi, Dong Liu, Peng Qi
papers.evidence: 用于机器人导航的视觉语言程序化推理与上下文感知奖励建模
papers.tldr: 现有的机器人血管介入导丝导航方法依赖静态奖励函数，无法适应复杂的解剖结构和任务进展。为此，本文提出视觉-语言程序推理（VL-PR）框架，集成多模态大模型作为程序推理模块，通过实时视觉观察推断高层导航上下文，并动态调整奖励组件的重要性。在物理机器人平台上的实验表明，该方法增强了任务可靠性和导航效率。这一框架为复杂多任务内血管手术提供了可扩展的上下文感知奖励建模方案。
papers.abstract_en: Robotic-assisted endovascular interventions demand accurate, stable, and context-aware guidewire navigation in complex and patient-specific vascular anatomies. Despite recent advances in robotic precision and learning-based control, existing autonomous navigation methods remain limited by their reliance on static reward functions and the lack of explicit procedural reasoning regarding anatomical context and task progression. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a vision-language procedural reasoning (VL-PR) framework for autonomous guidewire navigation. The framework integrates a multimodal large language model (MLLM) as a procedural reasoning module that interprets real-time visual observations to infer high-level navigation contexts. Instead of generating low-level control commands, the inferred procedural insights enable context-aware reward adaptation by dynamically adjusting the importance of reward components across different navigation phases. This approach allows a single policy to resolve competing objectives and handle complex transitions while preserving a consistent global task goal. Experiments on a physical robotic platform across diverse vascular scenarios demonstrate enhanced task reliability and streamlined navigational efficiency, highlighting the advantages over static-reward methods and offering a scalable solution for complex and multi-task robotic endovascular procedures.

papers.title_en: Technical Report of RoboSpatial Challenge at CVPR 2026: Selective Reasoning Activation and Reference-Frame Disambiguation for Embodied Spatial Reasoning
papers.authors: Yuxiang Xie, Qi Lv, Jianming Xing, Zijian Hong, Xiang Deng, Weili Guan, Liqiang Nie
papers.evidence: 使用VLM进行具身空间推理，适用于导航任务
papers.tldr: 视觉语言模型在通用感知方面表现出色，但在具身空间推理中常因缺乏深度推理和视角歧义而表现不佳。为此，RoboSpatialBrain基于RoboBrain2.5，提出两种免训练的推理时机制：一是强制<think>前缀激活与任务后提示，引导模型对上下文和兼容性任务进行深度逐步推理；二是显式参考帧重定向管道，消除相机与物体坐标系间的歧义，如“向左”指令的视角理解。此外，还探索了微调兼容性数据并分析提示与其交互以优化性能。在CVPR 2026 RoboSpatial挑战赛的RoboSpatial-Home测试中，该方法以80.9%成功率高居榜首，验证了其有效性。该工作表明，无需重新训练，仅通过推理时策略即可大幅提升预训练模型的空间推理能力，为具身智能提供高效实用方案。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models achieve strong general perception but often struggle with the spatial reasoning required for embodied tasks. We present RoboSpatialBrain, our submission to the RoboSpatial Challenge at the Embodied Reasoning in Action Workshop, CVPR 2026, built on RoboBrain2.5-8B-NV. RoboSpatialBrain combines two training-free, inference-time mechanisms: a forced <think> prefix activation strategy paired with a task-specific post-prompt that elicits deliberate reasoning on context and compatibility tasks, and an explicit reference-frame redirection pipeline that resolves camera-centric and object-centric ambiguity for context tasks. We additionally explore fine-tuning RoboBrain2.5 on compatibility data and present a detailed analysis of its interaction with prompting. RoboSpatialBrain achieved first place in the RoboSpatial Challenge, with an overall success rate of 80.9\% on RoboSpatial-Home. Code is available at https://github.com/YuxiangXie2003/RoboSpatialBrain.

papers.title_en: Rank-Aware Hyperbolic Alignment for Vision-Language Dataset Distillation
papers.authors: Jongoh Jeong, Sun-Kyung Lee, Kuk-Jin Yoon
papers.evidence: 视觉语言数据集蒸馏技术，可高效训练对比视觉语言模型，适用于VLN任务
papers.tldr: 视觉语言数据集蒸馏旨在压缩大规模图文对为少量合成样本以高效训练对比模型。现有方法在欧氏空间强制全维对齐，但图文相关性低秩导致限制过强。本文提出秩感知双曲对齐（RAHA），将表示提升至双曲空间并采用非对称目标实现测地线对齐，同时正则化残差子空间保留模态私有多样性。在基准上，RAHA在固定预算下实现了有竞争力的跨模态检索和更好的迁移指标。该方法通过显式控制对齐容量与层级几何，为数据集蒸馏提供了新视角。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language dataset distillation (VLDD) compresses a large image-text paired dataset into a small set of synthetic pairs that can efficiently train contrastive vision-language models under strict data and compute budgets. Most existing methods match expert trajectories or cross-modal statistics, yet still enforce full-dimensional alignment in a Euclidean embedding space. This is often overly restrictive due to rank-deficient image--text correlation, with shared semantics concentrated in a low-dimensional range and remaining variation spread across a weakly correlated residual subspace. LoRS relaxes alignment at the similarity level by low-rank factorization, but does not explicitly control dominant alignment capacity and structure in the representation space. We thus propose a rank-aware hyperbolic alignment (RAHA) that combines hierarchical geometry with explicit alignment-capacity control. RAHA lifts multimodal representations to hyperbolic space and optimizes distilled pairs with asymmetric objectives that enforce geodesic alignment in the shared range while regularizing the residual subspace to preserve modality-private diversity and improve transfer robustness. Experiments on benchmarks show that RAHA demonstrates competitive cross-modal retrieval and improved transfer indicators under fixed budgets.

papers.title_en: M2Note: Continual Evolution of Vision Language Models via Mistake Notebook Learning
papers.authors: Haiwen Li, Jing Tang, Rui Chen, Lei Sun, Xiangxiang Chu
papers.evidence: 通过错误笔记学习实现视觉语言模型的持续进化
papers.tldr: VLM在推理中仍有重复失败，如跳过视觉检查、误用规则和幻觉。M2Note提出免训练的持续进化框架，将失败轨迹转化为主题-指导笔记，通过多模态RAG检索并附加上下文来避免错误。在六个基准上持续改进，成本低且与CoT互补。支持自进化和跨模型进化，无需权重更新。
papers.abstract_en: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in multimodal reasoning tasks, yet they still suffer from recurring failures, such as skipping key visual checks, misapplying domain rules, and hallucinating unsupported concepts. Most existing solutions rely on supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), which are expensive to iterate and can be brittle under distribution shift. To this end, we propose Multimodal Mistake Notebook Learning (M2Note), a training-free continual evolution framework that externalizes learning into an editable memory. M2Note transforms failed trajectories into compact subject-guidance notes: the subject summarizes the underlying domain and concept, while the guidance provides actionable verification steps that can be reused in future inference. At test time, M2Note retrieves relevant notes via multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and appends them to the model context, steering reasoning away from previously observed pitfalls. To stabilize continual evolution, we adopt batch-level post-verification with rollback, which commits notebook edits only if they improve performance on the same batch, reducing noisy updates and preventing regressions. M2Note supports both self-evolving, where the same VLM acts as solver and supervisor, and cross-model evolving, where a stronger supervisor guides a weaker solver, enabling capability transfer without weight updates. Experiments on six multimodal reasoning benchmarks show consistent improvements across domains and backbones, while achieving strong cost and sample efficiency and remaining complementary to Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting.

papers.title_en: Guided Action Flow: Q-Guided Inference for Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.authors: Liuhaichen Yang, Zhuang Jiang, Chenchao Sheng, Zezhi Tang
papers.evidence: 带有指导的视觉-语言-动作策略用于机器人控制
papers.tldr: 流匹配VLA策略通过迭代传输生成机器人动作，允许在不重训基础策略下进行测试时引导。本文提出Guided Action Flow，保持预训练SmolVLA冻结，使用从真实成败轨迹学习的动作评论家，通过动作梯度引导逆向流采样。在LIBERO操作任务上，单任务评论家将成功率从68%提升至82%，从82%提升至86%；多任务评论家提升验证成功率从46%到56%，测试集从65%到67.5%。结果表明Q引导推理可行，但评论家泛化与不确定性感知仍为主要瓶颈。
papers.abstract_en: Flow-matching vision-language-action policies generate robot action chunks through an iterative transport process, creating an opportunity for test-time guidance without retraining the base policy. We study this opportunity in Guided Action Flow, an inference-time framework that keeps a pretrained SmolVLA policy frozen and uses a learned action-chunk critic to guide its reverse-time flow sampler. The critic is trained from real success and failure rollouts, can condition on task-description features from the frozen SmolVLA language pathway, and is used only through action gradients during sampling. We evaluate the approach on LIBERO manipulation tasks. A single-task critic improves success from 68.0% to 82.0% on one seed window and from 82.0% to 86.0% on another. A multi-family task-description critic improves validation success from 46.0% to 56.0%, while the locked held-out test gain is positive but modest, from 65.0% to 67.5%. These results support the feasibility of Q-guided inference for frozen flow-matching VLA policies, while showing that critic generalization and uncertainty-aware guidance remain the central bottlenecks.
